people.name: Helen Brandt
people.role: Head of Retail Deposits (business owner of savings products)
people.style: Warm, precise about contracts, slightly impatient with IT jargon.
knows: SV1 is Heritage Savings, sold only until 2008; every SV1 account was opened before 2009.

Heritage Savings contracts guarantee interest on a 30/360 day count: the 31st of a month accrues nothing, and the last day of February accrues up to day 30 (3 days in a 28-day February). Every other interest-bearing product (SV2 savings, MMA money market) is actual/365, and the bank uses 365 even in leap years.
SV1 must stay its own product and must never be converted to SV2. In 2016 an IT change tried to merge them; it caused a regulatory complaint and customer refunds.
Next quarter the bank launches 'Heritage Plus', product code SV3, for loyal Heritage customers. It keeps exactly the Heritage contract terms (30/360), with a different rate table.
Maintenance fee policy is unchanged from legacy: checking accounts below $500.00 at month end pay $5.00.

people.name: Owen Achterberg
people.role: Secretary of the Retail Banking Product Committee

knows.text: The committee is reviewing the overdraft fee for the new system; there is no decision yet.
Decision PC-2025-14 (board approved): with the new system the overdraft fee drops from $35.00 to $25.00 per overdraft event. It is an approved deviation from legacy.
PC-2025-14 is so far the only approved deviation from legacy behaviour; everything else must match the legacy batch.
The committee is discussing a monthly cap on overdraft fees; nothing is decided yet.

Decision PC-2025-21 (approved in sprint 4 of LIGHTHOUSE, effective with go-live): overdraft fees are capped at 3 per statement month, so the most a customer pays in overdraft fees in one month is $75.00. It amends PC-2025-14.
These two are the only approved deviations from legacy behaviour; everything else must match the legacy batch.

people.name: Mei Lin
people.style: Exact, cites findings; firm about scope.
knows: Regulatory finding RF-2025-07: full account numbers must never appear in application logs, batch reports or audit records; mask to the last 4 digits (for example ******1234).
Customer statements are exempt from masking; anything else that leaves the bank (exports, partner files) is not exempt.
Every change to an account balance needs an audit record: who or what, when, before, after, and the masked account.

people.name: Daniel Okoro
people.role: Finance architecture lead, Office of the CFO

knows.text: The program office told engineering to use long minor units (cents) for money. The CFO's office is reviewing that for the phase-2 multi-currency FX accounts.

In sprint 1 the program office told engineering to use long minor units (cents). That guidance was replaced in sprint 3 by directive CFO-2025-03: every monetary amount is java.math.BigDecimal with scale 4, because multi-currency FX accounts arrive in phase 2.

knows: Rounding to cents happens only where business rules require it: interest posting and fees.
The phase-2 FX partner API will exchange amounts as decimal strings with 4 fractional digits.

people.name: Carla Mendes
people.style: Practical, talks about retries and timeouts.
knows: The mobile app retries a transfer after a 10-second timeout, up to 3 times within 2 minutes, reusing the same channel reference (TXN-REF) with a new TXN-ID.
Starting next month the branch teller channel will also send TXN-REFs, and it retries deposits the same way.
A reference reused on a later business day is a genuine new request from the customer, not a retry.

people.name: Pat Quinn
people.role: Mainframe operations consultant (ran the nightly batch for 20 years, part-time now)
people.style: Chatty, full of war stories, but accurate.
knows: The nightly batch runs every calendar day including weekends and holidays.

Legacy dates are Julian YYDDD with a century window in DATEUTIL: YY below 70 means 20YY, otherwise 19YY. A handful of accounts really opened in 1968 and 1969 show as 2068 and 2069; the business decided years ago to leave them as they are, and the new system must reproduce legacy, not fix them silently.

XFERPROC has a 'channel retry guard': a non-blank TXN-REF already posted earlier the same business day is rejected with reason DUP; rejected transactions don't count, and a reference on a new day posts normally.
Interest accrues daily truncated to 6 decimals and is posted at month end with banker's rounding (round half to even) to cents.
